title: Essential Dashlets: MVP Cut Plan & Backstop Strategy
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Summary: Narrow the console MVP surface to an "essential dashlets" set to meet alpha launch date while preserving core troubleshooting and cost-awareness for customers. This PRD doc records scope trims, acceptance gates, and backstop behaviors so engineering, design, and SRE have a single source of truth for decisions and trade-offs.

Context: Our original telemetry plan included an expansive set of dashboard cards, deep trace exploration, and a cost breakdown explorer. Given resource constraints and performance risk, we are reducing the initial surface to: (1) two lightweight dashboard dashlets (Route Health and Token Cost Summary), (2) basic trace sampling with linkouts to logs, and (3) a compact cost-per-route summary instead of the full interactive cost explorer. The goal is to ship an actionable, low-latency console experience that supports troubleshooting and cost visibility for early customers.

Goals:
- Ensure alpha customers can identify route regressions and cost spikes within the console.
- Keep additional server-side telemetry ingestion and query complexity minimal to preserve latency SLOs.
- Provide deterministic fallback UI when heavy data is unavailable (degraded-mode).

Out of scope for MVP: full trace flame graphs, deep query/filters on cost explorer, long-retention historical charts (>30d), and per-token detailed tokenization breakdowns.
scope_changes: Removed: Interactive cost explorer (deferred to v2). Rationale: high QPS on cost aggregation and heavy query paths would push infra and risk SLA misses.

Kept but trimmed: Tracing surface reduced to sampled trace linkouts and a single 'slowest-span' indicator instead of span-level exploration. Rationale: preserves triage path while avoiding heavy trace storage UI.
Consolidated: Dashboard card set collapsed to two dashlets (Route Health, Token Cost Summary) with drill-through to logs and raw request preview only for P1 routes.
Introduced backstop: Degraded render mode that shows cached snapshots and explanatory banners when live aggregation exceeds latency threshold or quota.
Telemetry contract: Limit initial retention to 30 days for aggregated metrics and 7 days for raw traces to reduce storage costs and query surface for MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Route Health dashlet shows per-route 95th latency, error rate, and request volume for top 25 routes and updates within 60s for live traffic.
Token Cost Summary shows aggregated cost per-route (USD estimate) and delta vs 24h baseline; calculations match the billing-sim test dataset within 3%.
Tracing: for sampled requests, console shows a single trace summary row with latency, top span name, and a link to raw trace JSON in S3. Linking works in >95% of sampled traces in staging.

Degraded Mode: when aggregation queries exceed configured latency threshold (2000ms), the UI displays cached snapshot with timestamp and disables interactive filters; QA verifies fallback appears in simulated overload.
Performance: dashboard initial render (first paint) must be <1200ms on 90th percentile medium-sized accounts in staging environment.
Documentation: update console-telemetry-runbook and quickstart page with the trimmed telemetry contract, rollout plan, and known limitations for GA.
implementation_notes: Backend: add a lightweight aggregation endpoint that precomputes daily and 1h buckets for the two dashlets; reuse existing metrics pipeline to avoid new storage tiers.
Tracing: use existing sampled-span export to S3 and add console link builder; avoid adding a heavy trace UI component for MVP.
Frontend: create generic 'dashlet' component (thin) with props for refresh cadence and cache-timestamp display to simplify future card additions.
Rollout: feature-flag the entire dashlet bundle and the degraded-mode behavior; start with 5 pilot customers then ramp to all alpha accounts after validation.
Backstop: implement an automated job to capture and store hourly snapshots used by degraded-mode if live queries fail.
risks: Reduced feature set may disappoint early customers expecting deep investigation tools—mitigate with proactive communication and clear 'coming soon' messaging.
Aggregation errors could cause mismatches vs billing; mitigate with billing-sim dataset checks and cross-team validation with finance telemetry owners.
If degraded-mode auto-engages too often, it will erode trust; set conservative thresholds and run load tests in staging before rollout.
